demand_analysis.distribution_type: Mixed (zero-inflated, approximately normal on non-zero days)

safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Increase SAP safety lead time from 0.0 to 1.49 days

narrative: Material PL3__M41AAE85 exhibits intermittent, high-volume demand (mean 30,928 units/day, CV=1.44) over 218 working days from March 2025 to March 2026, with zero-demand days comprising ~23.5% of observations. Lead times are short (mean ~1.0 day) but moderately volatile (CV=0.91), driven almost entirely by transport variability. The current SAP safety stock of 15,900 units is insufficient for a 95% service level; the optimised (r,Q) policy raises safety stock to 50,144 units and sets a reorder point of 81,204 units with an EOQ-derived order quantity of 169,671 units, fully utilising available storage capacity of 219,815 units.
warnings: Storage capacity binds: safety_stock (50,144) + order_quantity (169,671) = 219,815 == max_storage_units (219,815.507). No buffer for demand spikes during lead time.
Current SAP safety stock (15,900) is ~68% below the model-recommended level (50,144) for 95% SL.
Intermittent demand (CV=1.44) — normal approximation for safety stock may underestimate tail risk on high-demand days.

research_insights.selection_rationale: High-volume continuous demand with moderately stable lead times and a well-defined EOQ makes the (r,Q) policy optimal. The fixed order quantity minimises total annual replenishment cost (ordering + holding), while the reorder point set at mean lead-time demand plus safety stock absorbs stochastic lead-time variability to achieve the 95% cycle service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is fully consumed by the recommended policy (SS + OQ = 219,815 units ≈ max_storage_units). Any upward revision of safety stock or service level target is infeasible without expanding storage. During periods of above-average demand, the hard storage ceiling prevents holding additional buffer inventory, exposing the supply chain to stockout risk if a long lead time (>2 days) coincides with elevated demand.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ (7,950) + safety_stock (50,144) = 58,094 units, which is well within the 219,815.5 unit storage limit. No MOQ-capacity infeasibility exists.
